claims.text: Directional thermomechanical treatment of the as-cast HEA will induce aligned nanoscale lamellae.
The aligned nanoscale lamellae will form continuous thermal-conduction pathways.
These pathways will enhance heat-transfer capability.
The treatment will not degrade structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
The initial intermediate-layer HEA has a largely equiaxed or randomly oriented microstructure.
The initial HEA is optimized for high strength and ductility.
The initial HEA has limited thermal conductivity.
Controlled rolling followed by annealing can reorient and align nanoscale lamellae or conductive phases along the primary heat-flux direction.
The treatment promotes microstructural anisotropy with high-conduction regions parallel to the heat flux.
Alignment of high-conduction regions parallel to heat flux enhances thermal conduction.
The HEA matrix will retain load-bearing strength and resistance to thermal stresses after directional processing.
The treated alloy will have noticeably higher thermal conductivity than the current intermediate layer.
The treated alloy will show no significant loss of mechanical strength.
The treated alloy will show no significant loss of microstructural stability.
The baseline's limited heat-transfer capability is caused by its non-optimized isotropic microstructure.
The intervention is expected to be effective only at approximately 1000°C or above under high mechanical and thermal loading.
More extreme thermal cycling or operational stresses may destabilize the aligned microstructure and diminish the treatment's effectiveness.

The hypothesis can be tested by comparing directionally treated and conventionally processed control samples at approximately 1000°C under cyclic mechanical loading in a plasma-simulation environment.
Thermal conductivity, tensile properties, fracture toughness, and lamellar alignment are measurable experimental outcomes.
Failure to obtain statistically significant thermal-conductivity improvement, or observation of marked mechanical degradation, would falsify the hypothesis.
